Bug_Title: Beans in "@Configuration" class should have different names
Bug_Details:
Naming conventions play a crucial role in maintaining code clarity and readability. The uniqueness of bean names in Spring configurations is vital
to the clarity and readability of the code. When two beans share the same name within a configuration, it is not obvious to the reader which bean is
being referred to. This leads to potential misunderstandings and errors.
Bug_Explanation: Two beans in the Spring configuration class have been named'myBean'. This is a bug because the names of beans in a configuration class should be unique.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case 'testShowBugMethod' expects the'showBug' method to return the map from the second bean, not the first one. However, as both beans are named the same ('myBean'), the'showBug' method is returning the map from the first bean, not the second one.
